instantiated_cells.justification: The statutes prohibit anyone from lobbying 'as a lobbyist' unless licensed and authorized, and define 'lobbyist' as an individual paid by a principal whose duties include lobbying (subject to a 5-days-per-reporting-period threshold), effectively requiring paid lobbyists who meet the definition to be licensed/registered as lobbyists.
Lobbyist licenses expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year, requiring renewal on a biennial (24-month) cycle.
Lobbyists must file a license application to be licensed, while principals separately must file a registration statement once lobbying expenditures exceed $500, making them independent filers.
The lobbyist license application is required to include a social security number (or an oath of no SSN) and be signed, but no photograph requirement is stated.
Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees are exempt from specified lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity.

An agency that files a statement under § 13.695 and named officials are not subject to several general lobbying requirements (including licensing/registration/reporting) except as provided in § 13.695, creating a partial exemption for government agencies.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text includes a 10-day change-notification rule for agencies (Wis. Stat. § 13.695(2)) but does not specify any deadline for lobbyists to notify the board of changes to their own license/registration information.

The statute requires licensing/authorization before engaging in lobbying (Wis. Stat. § 13.66) but does not state a numeric 'days after first lobbying' deadline for the lobbyist to register; thus the requested day-count cannot be derived.
